pages.title: Documentation
pages.description: Choose a standalone component, bounded data source, smart region, or optional agent path.
pages.body:
Choose the smallest integration that serves the task. Every path keeps application identity, authorization, and business execution in your host.

Standalone component

Render one owned element with ordinary properties and native events.

Local records

Evaluate bounded in-memory records without a model or provider.

HTTP application service

Connect an application-owned ADC service with explicit principal and source policy.

Smart region

Present named outputs through a validated adaptive region.

Optional agent

Add MCP or BYOK only when the host grants the required capability.

Concepts

Learn Catalog, Task, Result, Experience, meaning, scope, grain, and lineage.

Integration

Use the shared web implementation through vanilla, React, Vue, or SSR.

Production

Review accessibility, authorization, performance, SSR, migration, and troubleshooting.

Component catalog

Browse 71 real entries with executable examples and source-derived API metadata.

Release status

Aeliqo 0.1.0 is the current stable rewrite. Its six public packages are @aeliqo/core, @aeliqo/runtime, @aeliqo/web, @aeliqo/agent, @aeliqo/devtools, and @aeliqo/react. They are published on npm from one verified source revision. Historical npm versions use a different API.

pages.title: Choose an integration path
pages.description: Choose standalone, local, HTTP, region, or optional agent integration.
pages.body:
Your application supplies records, identity, routes, and business actions. Choose one bounded path before composing them.

Standalone

One component, no evaluator.

Local

Bounded records and a local evaluator.

HTTP

Application service and authenticated source policy.

Region

Validated task outputs and adaptive presentation.

Agent

Optional MCP or BYOK assistance.

Install the stable packages

Install the exact 0.1.0 packages used by your application. A basic web integration uses the matching core, runtime, and web packages.

npm install @aeliqo/core@0.1.0 @aeliqo/runtime@0.1.0 @aeliqo/web@0.1.0

The web package uses Lit and requires the matching Aeliqo runtime. React applications can also install @aeliqo/react@0.1.0. Historical npm releases are a separate, incompatible lineage; follow the 0.1 migration guide rather than substituting them.

Render a collection

What the application owns

Keep authenticated identity, source access, routes, and business execution in your application. A component’s scope label explains the supplied records; it does not authorize access to them.

Next steps

Use framework integration for React and Vue, or connect the local evaluator or application HTTP service.

pages.title: Standalone component
pages.description: Render one Aeliqo element directly with host-owned data and native events.
pages.body:
Use a standalone element when the application already has the data and interaction model. No planner, agent, or Region is required.

Use the direct web entry

Import the individual element from @aeliqo/web, register its custom-element name once, and assign structured properties from application code. The component does not fetch records or authorize access.

What to provide

  • Stable identity fields when the component supports selection.
  • Explicit scope and result metadata for data views.
  • Native or typed custom events handled by the application.

What to verify

Exercise loading, empty, partial, stale, and error states alongside the ready state. Keep essential comparisons and keyboard paths available at narrow widths.

Continue with the framework integration guide or inspect the component catalog.

pages.title: Local records
pages.description: Evaluate bounded application-owned records with the reusable local service.
pages.body:
Use the local path for bounded snapshots, local demonstrations, and applications that already own the data fetch.

Boundary

The runtime local service plans and executes only supported canonical operations over the supplied snapshot. It enforces row, byte, message, time, and column budgets; it is not an unbounded browser database download.

Keep host authority

The host supplies the authenticated principal, source policy, and permitted records. Discovery describes fields and capabilities; it does not grant execution access.

Result handling

Carry query, revision, scope, grain, completeness, precision, and lineage with the result. Cancel outstanding work and clear retained materialized data when access is revoked.

For a server-backed source, use HTTP application service. For a validated adaptive surface, use smart region.

pages.title: HTTP application service
pages.description: Connect an application-owned ADC service with explicit authentication and source policy.
pages.body:
Use HTTP when the application service must keep source access and authenticated execution on the server.

Separate description from execution

The ADC path carries catalog description, a validated query plan, and bounded result delivery as separate stages. The server injects the principal and source policy; a wire field never establishes authority.

Bound the transport

Reject malformed sequences, stale revisions, unsupported operations, over-budget requests, and unauthorized scope. Cancellation must stop outstanding work, and partial completeness must remain visible.

Application responsibilities

Own authentication, route protection, server credentials, business rules, and deployment. Do not put credentials in browser bundles, URLs, or exported task documents.

See data semantics for result identity and production considerations for operational checks.

pages.title: Smart region
pages.description: Present named outputs through a validated adaptive region without hiding required comparisons.
pages.body:
Use a Region when a task has named outputs and the presentation must adapt within explicit semantics, scope, accessibility, and host constraints.

Declare the task

Name each output and its grain. Keep output dependencies, visual containment, and typed interaction links distinct. A form or presentation may be queryless.

Evaluate before presenting

Inspect the validated Result, then commit a presentation plan with current revisions and authority. A failed proposal preserves the current authorized interface; revoked data is cleared.

Adapt without dropping meaning

Responsive layout may change, but an essential comparison, scope label, keyboard operation, or data state must not disappear. Claims in titles and tooltips require evidence in the correct result scope.

Start with the four public concepts, then review the support and lifecycle limits.

pages.title: Optional agent
pages.description: Add MCP or BYOK assistance only through the host capability boundary.
pages.body:
Agent assistance is optional. Manual code and ordinary clicks remain first-class paths and do not call a model.

Use the same typed dispatcher

MCP, BYOK, and experimental WebMCP proposals pass through the same bounded tool and binder contracts as manual composition. The host owns credentials, grants, budgets, cancellation, and egress.

Contain proposals

Shape-valid or approved does not prove business truth or intent correctness. Keep outcomes explicit: bound, needs-choice, needs-meaning, unsupported, denied, invalid, or stale. Do not expose private chain-of-thought or model text as evidence.

Keep the fallback usable

When a provider is unavailable, preserve the current authorized interface and offer a manual route. Retry within a finite budget and stop when no progress is possible.

Read the detailed protocol notes and production boundary.

pages.title: Four public concepts
pages.description: Catalog, Task, Result, and Experience connect application intent to a validated interface.
pages.body:
The four concepts keep data semantics, the requested work, its evidence, and the user’s experience explicit.

Catalog

The Catalog describes entities, identity, field types, relationships, meanings, and source capabilities. Discovery describes a source; it does not grant execution capability.

Task

A Task declares named outputs and operations. Outputs can have different grains. A form or presentation can be queryless. Output dependencies, the visual containment tree, and interaction links are separate structures.

Result

A Result identifies evaluated output with revision, query and scope digests, grain, completeness, precision, and lineage. Row data is materialized through the runtime. Selection refers to stable entity identity rather than a visible row position.

Experience

Experience constrains presentation and adaptation alongside permissions, accessibility, and task requirements. A narrow screen must preserve essential comparisons and operations.

Evaluate, then present

Evaluation and inspection do not commit an interface. The host accepts a validated presentation with current revision and authority checks. Failed proposals preserve the current authorized interface; revoked data is cleared.

pages.title: Data and meaning
pages.description: One versioned definition graph for developer code, Studio, and optional AI proposals.
pages.body:
Define business meaning once, in a form that can be checked, evaluated, and reviewed.

Start from the schema

Use the typed meaning builder to refer to an existing entity and field, compose registered functions, and define a meaning. An unknown field or incompatible input returns a diagnostic. A well-typed expression can still express the wrong business intent.

Keep ownership explicit

Developers may ship reviewed, built-in meanings from code. Users do not need to redefine them in Studio or approve them for every question. AI drafts cannot silently replace a code-owned definition. Registration preserves immutable versions and reports conflicts.

Check the semantics

Review identity, grain, fanout, units, null and zero behavior, temporal policy, fixed versus live cohorts, precision, and completeness. A count of records and a count of distinct people can answer different questions.

Activation is a host decision

Read, evaluate, meaning activation, presentation, action execution, and model egress have independent grants. An AI origin label never grants authority.

See the developer integration examples for the compiled manual path.

pages.title: Connect application data
pages.description: Use the reusable local evaluator or the application-owned ADC HTTP path.
pages.body:
Choose a bounded local source or an application service. The application controls access in both cases.

Local records

The runtime local data service plans and executes supported canonical queries over supplied snapshots. It enforces row, byte, message, time, and column budgets. Use it for local records and demonstrations, not an unbounded browser download of a database.

Application HTTP service

The ADC HTTP path separates catalog description, query planning, and execution. The server supplies authenticated principal and source policy. Wire fields do not establish caller authority.

Results and updates

Result references carry query, revision, and scope identity. Cancellation stops outstanding work. Consumers reject malformed stream sequences and stale results. If access is revoked, clear retained materialized data.

Unsupported queries

Return a typed unsupported outcome when the source cannot execute a requested operation. Do not silently fetch more data or invent a server capability.

Local audit export

The runtime includes a bounded in-memory exporter for fixed plan, capability, cancellation, source, cache, renderer, and resource events. It rejects free-form messages, records, prompts, credentials, URLs, and identity fields. Your application owns collector scope, storage, transport, and access; the SDK performs no audit network or filesystem I/O.

pages.title: Framework integration
pages.description: Use the shared web implementation directly or through thin framework bindings.
pages.body:
Choose your application stack. Every option below uses the same Aeliqo web components, properties, and native events.

Vanilla JavaScript

Import the component you need, register it once, then assign structured values as properties.

import {AeliqoRecordListElement} from '@aeliqo/web/record-list';

customElements.define('aeliqo-record-list', AeliqoRecordListElement);
const list = document.querySelector('aeliqo-record-list');
list.rows = people;
list.columns = [{key: 'name', label: 'Name'}];
list.identity = ['id'];

React

Use the thin React wrapper when you want typed props and event callbacks in JSX.

import {RecordList} from '@aeliqo/react/record-list';

<RecordList
  rows={people}
  columns={[{key: 'name', label: 'Name'}]}
  identity={['id']}
  onSelectionChange={(event) => setSelected(event.detail.identity)}
/>

Vue

Configure Vue to treat aeliqo-* tags as custom elements, bind objects with :, and handle native events with @. No separate Vue renderer is required.

Server rendering

The web server entry produces declarative shadow roots. React has an explicit SSR integration entry. Verify hydration, forms, focus, and event handling in your deployment environment.

Start with the record-list quickstart, then use the component catalog for runnable examples and generated API details.

pages.title: Optional agents and protocols
pages.description: Manual, MCP, BYOK, and experimental WebMCP share one capability dispatcher.
pages.body:
Add AI assistance when it helps the task. Ordinary clicks, typing, and resizing do not call a model.

MCP

The optional MCP entries use the official SDK and support tested stdio and HTTP flows. Host authentication, tool discovery, cancellation, budgets, and current grants remain enforced at the endpoint.

Bring your own model

The bounded model loop projects approved tools to a host-supplied provider. The OpenAI adapter is a separate server-side entry. Configure a host backend reference; never put a provider secret in a public bundle, URL, or browser storage.

Experimental WebMCP

The adapter detects the browser surface. The tested Chrome default configuration does not expose it. An experimental Chrome flag exposes a native API; simulated tests and native-browser observations are recorded separately.

Failure containment

Model proposals are untrusted. Outcomes distinguish bound, needs-choice, needs-meaning, unsupported, denied, invalid, and stale. Shape validation cannot prove business intent. Model text remains an unverified draft unless separately grounded.

Current limits

Protocol, deterministic-loop, and bounded live-provider integration evidence are recorded separately. Provider compatibility does not establish model accuracy or business-intent correctness, and this page makes no such guarantee.

pages.title: Production considerations
pages.description: Review authorization, accessibility, lifecycle, performance, and release compatibility.
pages.body:
Permissions and model egress

Keep the authenticated principal and host grants outside proposal content. Check each effect independently, including read, evaluation, meaning activation, presentation, action, and model egress. Recheck current scope around asynchronous work.

Accessibility

Component tests cover keyboard behavior, focus, forms, forced colors, and automated accessibility checks. Full release manual assistive technology and device evidence is still pending. Test your composition with real users and assistive technology; no single badge covers every use.

Performance

Use individual component imports for small embeds. Load the planner, agent, and inspector only when needed. Preserve bounded materialization and query budgets. Published measurements describe a specific workload and environment, not a universal row or pixel guarantee.

Version migration

The stable rewrite is 0.1.0 under @aeliqo/core, @aeliqo/runtime, @aeliqo/web, @aeliqo/react, @aeliqo/agent, and @aeliqo/devtools. It is not an automatic upgrade from historical higher semantic versions. Read the migration guide and pin the complete Aeliqo package set to one version.

Troubleshooting

For stale outcomes, refresh the exact revision and scope rather than retrying an old proposal. For unsupported queries, inspect the source capability. For a missing meaning, define or select the intended business definition. Provider retries must remain bounded.

pages.title: About Aeliqo
pages.description: An open-source framework for semantic, adaptive user interfaces.
pages.body:
Aeliqo connects application data and intent to ready-to-use interfaces.

The framework owns its primitives and 2D views, typed semantics, query and presentation validation, and optional agent plumbing. Applications own data, authentication, routes, and business execution.

The 0.1.0 source, package publication, and production deployment each carry separate evidence. Availability on one surface does not imply the others.

pages.title: License
pages.description: The framework and local developer tools use Apache-2.0.
pages.body:
Aeliqo’s runtime, complete component catalog, security and accessibility functionality, local Studio and testkit, and agent plumbing use Apache-2.0.

There is no safety paywall, license-network dependency, or artificial paid row cap. Future commercial organizational operation and support would use a separate service and license boundary; no hosted service, price, SLA, or customer demand is claimed for 0.1.0.

See the repository license, trademark guidelines, and dependency notices for the full terms.

pages.title: Privacy
pages.description: What this local preview stores and sends.
pages.body:
This preview uses synthetic demonstration data. Filtering runs locally. Browser monitoring and Google Analytics ship disabled and do not run in local previews, documentation examples, or SDK consumers.

A production host may separately enable bounded same-origin browser telemetry for the public HTTPS Aeliqo site. It sends only fixed service metadata and numeric aggregate page, error, navigation, and supported browser-performance observations; it excludes URLs, query strings, referrers, form content, user identifiers, and persistent session identifiers. Delivery is bounded and best-effort.

If a production host enables Google Analytics, the public site asks before loading it. The page event contains only the origin and path, not query or hash, and disables Google Signals, ad personalization, and client storage. Declining keeps it off. The consent choice is stored locally so the prompt is not repeated.

Your theme preference is stored in this browser when browser storage is available. Playground work is ephemeral unless you explicitly export it. Exported task documents must not contain provider credentials or raw sensitive rows.

Opening GitHub or another external link sends a request to that destination. A future host-configured model connection must disclose its egress and require the host’s separate permission.

pages.title: Security
pages.description: Host-controlled boundaries and responsible issue reporting.
pages.body:
Applications are responsible for authenticated identity, data access, route protection, and business actions. Aeliqo validates typed proposals and current grants at its boundaries; validation is not proof of business truth.

Do not include credentials, customer records, or exploit details in a public issue. Use GitHub private vulnerability reporting, verified enabled for the official repository on September 10, 2026. No monitored security email address or response-time SLA is claimed.

pages.title: Support
pages.description: Report reproducible issues against the exact package version.
pages.body:
For a reproducible non-sensitive issue, include the exact package versions, browser, framework, minimal fixture, expected behavior, and actual result.

The source repository is the public project reference. The open-source release does not promise a response time or commercial support agreement.

pages.title: Engineering notes
pages.description: Notes on the framework’s design and implementation.
pages.body:
Decisions behind the interface.

DESIGN NOTE · SEPTEMBER 9, 2026

Why four concepts are enough

Keeping application ownership clear while connecting data, intent, evidence, and experience.

pages.title: Why four concepts are enough
pages.description: Catalog, Task, Result, and Experience separate intent from execution and evidence.
pages.body:
An adaptive interface needs more than a layout suggestion. It needs to know what the data means, what work was requested, and what the result actually supports.

Start with ownership

The application already knows who the user is, which records they may access, and which actions are valid. Aeliqo should not become a second authority for those decisions. The host keeps them.

Describe the work

A Catalog captures the available entities and meanings. A Task names the required outputs and operations. Their structures let the evaluator detect unsupported requests and the presentation validator preserve required information.

Carry evidence forward

A Result carries scope, grain, precision, completeness, and lineage. Those details matter when a table becomes a chart or a user selects a record. A filtered count must not acquire a title that implies the whole population.

Adapt within constraints

Experience describes how the interface should behave alongside accessibility and task requirements. Adaptation can change a layout, but it cannot remove an essential comparison or bypass a permission.

This is the design of 0.1.0. Source, package, and deployment claims remain bound to their respective release evidence.

pages.title: Button
pages.description: Trigger one explicit action; native button semantics; disabled and pending never double-submit.
pages.body:
Trigger one explicit action; native button semantics; disabled and pending never double-submit.

Preview

Interactive preview requires JavaScript.

Code and required setup
import {
  AeliqoAvatarElement,
  AeliqoBadgeElement,
  AeliqoButtonElement,
  AeliqoGridElement,
  AeliqoHeadingElement,
  AeliqoIconButtonElement,
  AeliqoLinkElement,
  AeliqoScrollAreaElement,
  AeliqoSeparatorElement,
  AeliqoSplitPaneElement,
  AeliqoStackElement,
  AeliqoSurfaceElement,
  AeliqoTextElement,
  registerAeliqoElements,
} from "@aeliqo/web";



registerAeliqoElements();

const host = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#aeliqo-example") ?? (() => {
  const created = document.createElement("div");
  created.id = "aeliqo-example";
  (document.body ?? document.documentElement).append(created);
  return created;
})();

function createCatalogRoot(container: HTMLElement): HTMLElement {
  const root = document.createElement("div");
  root.dataset.catalogSourceRoot = "true";
  root.style.display = "grid";
  root.style.gap = "12px";
  container.append(root);
  return root;
}

function createCatalogElement<T extends HTMLElement>(tagName: string, container: HTMLElement): T {
  const element = document.createElement(tagName) as T;
  container.append(element);
  return element;
}

function appendSlottedText(root: HTMLElement, slot: string, textContent: string): void {
  const content = document.createElement("span");
  content.slot = slot;
  content.textContent = textContent;
  root.append(content);
}

const root = createCatalogRoot(host);
(((root) => {
		const element = createCatalogElement<AeliqoButtonElement>("aeliqo-button", root);
		element.label = "Save report";
		element.variant = "solid";
		element.type = "button";
	}))(root);

Input fixture

One primary action with a host-owned save request.

Expected result

A cancellable action proposal is emitted when the native button is activated.

Properties and host ownership

label, variant, size, type, disabled, pending. The host chooses the action type and pending state; the component never performs persistence.

States

ready, disabled, pending

Keyboard behavior

Tab, Enter, Space

Events

aeliqo-action

Purpose

A direct foundation primitive with native semantics and tokenized layout. Trigger one explicit action; native button semantics; disabled and pending never double-submit.

Do / don't

  • Do: use the declared properties, explicit fixture, and host-owned event boundary shown below.
  • Don't: treat the component as an authorization boundary, data source, or substitute for missing semantic evidence.

Dependencies

These entries are imports referenced by the selected component class or its class lineage; they are not inferred from package installation.

  • ./action-base.js
  • ./base.js
  • ./events.js
  • lit

Inspected repository source files: packages/web/src/foundation/action-base.ts, packages/web/src/foundation/base.ts, packages/web/src/foundation/button.ts.

Controlled and uncontrolled use

Public properties with source-declared construction initializers: disabled, pending, type, name, value, label, variant, size. These initial values do not establish a controlled or uncontrolled contract. Treat the component’s documented events and behavior tests as authoritative.

Semantic elements and accessibility hooks

These native elements and attributes are present in the selected class-lineage render source; the example and browser checks remain the authoritative behavior evidence.

  • aria-busy
  • aria-hidden
  • button

Sizing and adaptation

Selected class-lineage styles declare block-size, inline-size, max-inline-size, min-block-size. Conditional selectors and media queries determine their values. Browser behavior remains authoritative.

Performance boundary

  • No explicit source bound was found in the selected class lineage. Measure the composed workload in your environment.

		name.value = "Ada Lovelace";
		identity.append(name);
		const review = document.createElement("div");
		review.slot = "step-review";
		review.textContent = "Review the authorized values before commit.";
		element.append(identity, review);
	}))(root);

Source, freshness, completeness, provenance and unsupported claims displayed honestly.

Preview

Interactive preview requires JavaScript.

Code and required setup

  AeliqoComparisonElement,
  AeliqoDateRangeElement,
  AeliqoExplorerElement,
  AeliqoFormFlowElement,
  AeliqoInvestigationElement,

import type {ResultRef, Scalar, VisualizationBindingContext, VisualizationSpec} from "@aeliqo/core";
import type {AeliqoDataColumn, AeliqoDataScope, AeliqoFieldOption} from "@aeliqo/web/data";
import type {VisualizationDataset} from "@aeliqo/web/visualization";

const catalogRef: ResultRef = {
  id: "aeliqo-catalog-example",
  revision: "1",
  outputId: "people",
  queryDigest: "catalog-query",
  scopeDigest: "catalog-scope",
};
const catalogRows: readonly Readonly<Record<string, Scalar>>[] = [
  {id: "ada", name: "Ada Lovelace", team: "Research", date: "2026-09-08", amount: 120},
  {id: "lin", name: "Lin Chen", team: "Product", date: "2026-09-09", amount: 96},
  {id: "grace", name: "Grace Hopper", team: "Research", date: "2026-09-10", amount: 144},
];
const catalogColumns: readonly AeliqoDataColumn[] = [
  {key: "id", label: "ID", type: "text", sortable: true},
  {key: "name", label: "Name", type: "text", sortable: true},
  {key: "team", label: "Team", type: "text"},
  {key: "date", label: "Date", type: "date", sortable: true},
  {key: "amount", label: "Amount", type: "integer", align: "end"},
];
const catalogFields: readonly AeliqoFieldOption[] = [
  {id: "name", label: "Name", type: "text"},
  {id: "team", label: "Team", type: "text"},
  {id: "amount", label: "Amount", type: "integer"},
];
const catalogScope: AeliqoDataScope = {loaded: catalogRows.length, filteredTotal: catalogRows.length, populationDigest: catalogRef.scopeDigest, kind: "filtered", label: "Authorized people"};
const catalogVisualizationContext: VisualizationBindingContext = {results: []};
const catalogVisualizationDataset: VisualizationDataset = {result: catalogRef, rows: catalogRows};
const catalogVisualizationSpecs: Readonly<Record<"trend", VisualizationSpec>> = {trend: {version: "1", view: "trend", plot: {version: "1", root: {kind: "unit", mark: "line", result: catalogRef, missing: "gap", encoding: {x: {field: "date", scale: "temporal"}, y: {field: "amount", scale: "linear"}}}}}};

registerAeliqoElements();

const host = document.querySelector<HTMLElement>("#aeliqo-example") ?? (() => {
  const created = document.createElement("div");
  created.id = "aeliqo-example";
  (document.body ?? document.documentElement).append(created);
  return created;
})();

function createCatalogRoot(container: HTMLElement): HTMLElement {
  const root = document.createElement("div");
  root.dataset.catalogSourceRoot = "true";
  root.style.display = "grid";
  root.style.gap = "12px";
  container.append(root);
  return root;
}

function createCatalogElement<T extends HTMLElement>(tagName: string, container: HTMLElement): T {
  const element = document.createElement(tagName) as T;
  container.append(element);
  return element;
}

function appendSlottedText(root: HTMLElement, slot: string, textContent: string): void {
  const content = document.createElement("span");
  content.slot = slot;
  content.textContent = textContent;
  root.append(content);
}

const root = createCatalogRoot(host);
(((root) => {
		const element = createCatalogElement<AeliqoQualityPanelElement>("aeliqo-quality-panel", root);
		element.source = "People registry";
		element.freshness = "2026-09-09 09:00 UTC";
		element.completeness = "3 of 3 rows loaded";
		element.provenance = ["Authorized local snapshot", "Query: catalog-query"];
		element.unsupportedClaims = ["This view does not establish causation."];
		element.state = {
			source: element.source,
			freshness: element.freshness,
			completeness: element.completeness,
			provenance: element.provenance,
			unsupportedClaims: element.unsupportedClaims
		};
	}))(root);

pages.title: Search documentation
pages.description: Search Aeliqo documentation by title or description.
pages.body:
Search is progressively enhanced when JavaScript is available. Without it, this page remains a browsable list of documentation routes.

With JavaScript disabled, use your browser’s Find command after submitting the query.

  • DocumentationChoose a standalone component, bounded data source, smart region, or optional agent path.
  • Choose an integration pathChoose standalone, local, HTTP, region, or optional agent integration.
  • Standalone componentRender one Aeliqo element directly with host-owned data and native events.
  • Local recordsEvaluate bounded application-owned records with the reusable local service.
  • HTTP application serviceConnect an application-owned ADC service with explicit authentication and source policy.
  • Smart regionPresent named outputs through a validated adaptive region without hiding required comparisons.
  • Optional agentAdd MCP or BYOK assistance only through the host capability boundary.
  • Four public conceptsCatalog, Task, Result, and Experience connect application intent to a validated interface.
  • Data and meaningOne versioned definition graph for developer code, Studio, and optional AI proposals.
  • Connect application dataUse the reusable local evaluator or the application-owned ADC HTTP path.
  • Framework integrationUse the shared web implementation directly or through thin framework bindings.
  • Optional agents and protocolsManual, MCP, BYOK, and experimental WebMCP share one capability dispatcher.
  • Production considerationsReview authorization, accessibility, lifecycle, performance, and release compatibility.
  • Component catalog71 owned components, grouped by purpose.
  • ButtonTrigger one explicit action; native button semantics; disabled and pending never double-submit.
  • IconButtonNamed compact action with minimum target area; icon alone is never its accessible name.
  • LinkNavigate to an application-approved destination; preserve browser open-in-new-tab behavior.
  • TextRender trusted/plain text with locale and wrapping; no untrusted HTML interpolation.
  • HeadingPreserve logical document hierarchy independent of visual size.
  • BadgePresent a category/status with text as well as color.
  • AvatarDisplay optional identity image; fallback initials and privacy-safe alt policy.
  • SeparatorExpress visual or semantic separation without polluting keyboard order.
  • SurfaceProvide consistent bounded chrome; never impose dashboard cards on every control.
  • StackArrange children in logical reading order with tokenized spacing.
  • GridArrange responsive regions without changing semantic/focus order.
  • SplitPaneResize adjacent regions by pointer and keyboard while respecting minimum task requirements.
  • ScrollAreaPreserve native scrolling, focus visibility, zoom and platform affordances.
  • TextFieldLabel, description, validation, autocomplete and IME-safe controlled/uncontrolled value.
  • TextAreaMultiline editing preserves draft, selection and composition across unrelated updates.
  • NumberFieldLocale-aware editing separates display text from exact numeric value; do not silently round money.
  • CheckboxNative checked/indeterminate state; group ownership and submitted value are explicit.
  • RadioGroupOne selected option; native semantics or APG-equivalent keyboard behavior.
  • SwitchBinary setting with visible label; changing setting is not implicit business submission.
  • SelectBounded enumerated choice with native-first semantics; empty and unknown value are distinct.
  • ComboboxSearchable choice with APG behavior; stale remote options cannot overwrite current input.
  • DateFieldCalendar date rather than timezone-shifted timestamp; typed entry and picker agree.
  • DateRangeExplicit inclusive/exclusive boundaries, timezone/calendar policy and keyboard operation.
  • SliderBounded quantity with keyboard and text alternative; steps and units are declared.
  • SearchFieldExplicit/debounced query policy; composition input is not submitted mid-IME.
  • FileInputNative file selection; host owns upload and validation; no file bytes enter agent by default.
  • FieldGroupGroup related controls with legend, descriptions and coordinated validation.
  • FormNative submission semantics, draft validation, error summary and explicit host action; rerender never submits.
  • TabsNamed panels with stable selection; automatic activation only when latency permits.
  • BreadcrumbReversible context path; approved routes and current-location semantics.
  • PaginationStable cursor/page scope; loaded rows are not misrepresented as global selection.
  • MenuAction menu with focus return and keyboard behavior; no layout-generated business actions.
  • TreeNavHierarchical navigation with stable node identities, expansion and keyboard semantics.
  • TooltipSupplemental nonessential information; works on focus, dismisses, not the sole label.
  • PopoverContextual nonmodal surface with explicit focus/dismiss behavior and viewport containment.
  • DialogNative-first modal semantics, focus containment/return and escape policy.
  • DrawerInline or modal detail according to an explicit mode; do not mix the two focus models.
  • ToastBounded transient feedback; essential errors remain persistently available elsewhere.
  • AlertPersistent status/error with severity semantics and actionable recovery.
  • ProgressDeterminate or unknown progress honestly; no invented completion percentages.
  • SkeletonStable reserved geometry with reduced motion and a named loading state.
  • EmptyStateDistinguish no records, no matches, forbidden data, loading and failure.
  • MetricOne validated value or aggregate with units, scope and unavailable state.
  • DeltaExplicit compatible baseline; zero denominator and percentage-point versus relative change distinguished.
  • KeyValueLabeled facts with stable ordering, wrapping and semantic links.
  • DetailSelected entity facts including missing fields; record identity persists across views.
  • RecordListScannable records with identity-based selection and reachable additional fields.
  • CardCollectionRepeated compact records; preserve reading order, headings and bounded loading.
  • TableNative table first; separate interactive-grid mode; sorting, paging, selection, virtualization and precise values.
  • FilterBuilderTyped predicates, AND/OR/null handling, visible inherited scope and explicit query application.
  • SelectionSummaryDisclose selected identities or server predicate scope; never imply unobserved global selection.
  • TrendTemporal metric series, declared grain, gaps and exact accessible summaries.
  • BarComparable quantitative categories; baseline and negative values correctly represented.
  • AreaTemporal area/stack with compatible additive measures; reject misleading nonadditive stacking.
  • ScatterTwo quantitative axes, declared units, stable point selection and noncausal interpretation.
  • HistogramDeclared binning, count/density labeling and missing-population disclosure.
  • HeatmapTwo dimensions and one measure; accessible exact cell values and readable color key.
  • MatrixEntity-feature comparison preserving row/column association and useful comparison at narrow width.
  • RelationshipDeclared edges/cardinality only; deterministic bounded layout with accessible adjacency view.
  • TreeExplicit hierarchy, cycle validation, stable expansion and equivalent text navigation.
  • TreemapNonnegative additive hierarchy; area meaning and tiny-node access preserved.
  • TimelineDated events/intervals with timezone semantics, explicit overlaps and chronological alternative.
  • CalendarGridCalendar-aligned 2D values/events; locale week boundaries and noncolor exact values.
  • ExplorerFilter plus collection plus selected detail using shared parameter/selection state.
  • ComparisonA stable compare-set with compatible metrics and simultaneous comparison affordances.
  • BreakdownGroup a declared metric and inspect contributing records; recompute ratios from sufficient statistics.
  • InvestigationTrend, baseline, event timeline and detail; associations never imply causes.
  • SearchResultsQuery state, collection, scoped result count and details with stale-result protection.
  • RecordEditorExisting primitive form over a host-owned action with entity revision and explicit save/cancel.
  • FormFlowTask-based steps, draft persistence, validation and reversible navigation before commit.
  • QualityPanelSource, freshness, completeness, provenance and unsupported claims displayed honestly.
